task: Make the Text size/Margins slider cards more compact (reveal more of the display behind the drawer) and make the Text size slider feel perceptually even (log-scale mapping instead of linear pixels)

public/styles/settings.css.summary: Removed redundant stacked spacing between a range-field's label row and its slider: .range-head no longer has its own margin-bottom (was additive with .range-field's grid gap), .range-field's own gap/padding shrunk, .viewDrawer .settingsStack's gap between the two cards shrunk, and .sliderInput's own margin dropped from 1.25rem/0.75rem to 0.75rem/0.4rem (0.75rem is the actual minimum needed to clear the 2rem thumb's overflow past the 0.5rem track).

public/services/view-settings.js.summary: Added FONT_SIZE_SLIDER_MAX plus fontSizeFromSliderPosition/sliderPositionFromFontSize -- the font-size <input> now moves on a fine-grained linear position scale (0-1000) that maps exponentially onto the real 24-144px range, so equal drag distance is equal *percentage* change in size, not equal pixel change (fixes the 'jumps fast at first, slows down' feel of a linear px slider).

public/index.html.summary: #fontSize input's min/max/step changed from 24/144/4 (raw pixels) to 0/1000/1 (the new position scale).

public/controller/start-app.js.summary: The fontSize input's 'input' handler now converts the raw slider position through fontSizeFromSliderPosition before calling runtime.setFontSize -- runtime/state still only ever deal in real pixel values.

public/controller/view.js.summary: syncViewerControls now sets the fontSize input's value via sliderPositionFromFontSize(ctx.state.fontSize) instead of the raw px value, and sets aria-valuetext to the human-readable 'Npx' string since the raw slider value is no longer meaningful to assistive tech.

test/public/services/view-settings.test..summary: Added coverage for the new exponential mapping: endpoint round-trips, the midpoint being the geometric (not arithmetic) mean, and the last third of slider travel covering more pixels than the first third.
